newsitem.title: USA: Waterbury,Conn weighs $100 mln sewer upgrade-paper.
newsitem.headline: Waterbury,Conn weighs $100 mln sewer upgrade-paper.

text.p: Waterbury, Connecticut is about to go to bid on an upgrade of its sewage plant that is projected to cost up to $100 million, an expense local officals are trying to cut, the Hartford Courant said Monday.

The cost-cutting measures, which range from an accelerated construction schedule and a compromise on existing sewage treatment, which would mean that for 14 months of construction the city would pollute the Naugatuck more than it now does, could save about $13 million.

The paper said the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, which must rule on the city and state plans, is reviewing the proposal to bypass existing treatment processes during construction, a step not ordinarily allowed.
The project includes removing five dams on the river, which would allow migratory fish to travel upstream, and further improve water quality.
